MaxUpgradeLevel.rationale: `=> 0` (Beckon.cs:13) == the class attribute, so `is_upgradable` is False and Apotheosis/Armaments skip it.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Status, CardRarity.Status, TargetType.None)` (Beckon.cs:19-22) == cost 1 / STATUS / STATUS / NONE. Beckon declares NO CanonicalKeywords, so it is NOT Unplayable, and the sim correctly leaves `is_playable` at its True default -- a playable no-effect Status on both sides. The cost is a real 1, not the -1 sentinel the unplayable statuses use, so the ascenders_bane cost finding does not apply here.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: nothing -- the sim inlines 6 at the damage site (beckon.py:39)
CanonicalVars.issue: `new HpLossVar(6m)` (Beckon.cs:17) is a printed card var; the sim declares no `_hp_loss` in `_init_vars`, so `Card.base_hp_loss` (cards/base.py:202-210) returns its 0 default and the number 6 exists only as a literal inside `on_turn_end_in_hand`. A policy sees Beckon as a harmless 0-HP-loss status. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed DynamicVar with no corresponding `_`-attribute in `_init_vars`, so the sim's printed-number API reports the default and `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card wrongly for the policy. DORMANT for game fidelity (the dealt number is identical), LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnTurnEndInHand.rationale: `CreatureCmd.Damage(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.HpLoss.BaseValue, Unblockable | Unpowered | Move, this)` (Beckon.cs:26) == `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, 6, card=self, props=DamageProps.CARD_HP_LOSS)`; `CARD_HP_LOSS` is exactly that prop triple (valueprops.py:38). No dealer on either side. Unlike Bad Luck there is no Cmd.Wait, so the two bodies are step-for-step identical.

OnPlay.rationale: Beckon.cs declares no OnPlay, so playing it does nothing; the sim's abstract method is a `pass`. Because Beckon IS playable this is a reachable no-op on both sides, not dead code.

guards.what: the sim adds `is_unpowered = True` (beckon.py:26), which has no counterpart in Beckon.cs
guards.rationale: The verdict holds but NOT for the reason first recorded: `is_unpowered` has NINE readers in the sim, not one. Besides `DamageCmd.deal`'s prop inference (cmds.py:46-50) it is read at powers.py:116, 1260, 1385, 1911 and 3965, relics/the_boot.py:37, previews.py:157 and cards/thrash.py:44. Each is independently unreachable for Beckon, checked by execution rather than assumed: (1) cmds.py:46-50 is the `props is None` branch and Beckon's only damage passes `CARD_HP_LOSS` explicitly (beckon.py:39), so the inference never runs. (2) powers.py:116 (StrengthPower.modify_damage_additive), 1260 and 1385 (modify_damage_multiplicative) are dispatched only from inside `DamageCmd.deal`'s `if is_powered_attack(props):` gate (cmds.py:56-58); `CARD_HP_LOSS` is `UNBLOCKABLE | UNPOWERED | MOVE` (valueprops.py:38) and `is_powered_attack` is `MOVE in props and UNPOWERED not in props` (valueprops.py:47-49), which evaluates False -- the whole modifier dispatch is skipped, so those three never see Beckon. (3) powers.py:1911 (VigorPower.before_attack) and 3965 (before_attack) fire only from combat.py:476-479, which brackets the play in `is_attack = card.card_type == CardType.ATTACK`; Beckon is a STATUS, and its damage is not a card play at all -- it comes from `on_turn_end_in_hand`. (4) relics/the_boot.py:37 is guarded by `if dealer is not self.player or target is self.player: return amount` (the_boot.py:34-35) and Beckon deals with NO dealer to the player, so both disjuncts hold and it returns before the read. (5) previews.py:157 is preceded by `base = card_base_damage(...); if base is None: return None` (previews.py:154-156); Beckon declares no `_damage` and no `calc_damage`, so `base_damage` returns its `getattr(self, "_damage", None)` default of None (cards/base.py:191-196) and the function returns before line 157. (6) cards/thrash.py:44 runs only on a victim drawn from `[c for c in ctx.player.hand if c.card_type == CT.ATTACK]` (thrash.py:58); Beckon is a STATUS and can never be that victim. So the flag is inert on this card at every site, and adding it to a card Beckon.cs does not mark is harmless -- but it is inert by nine separate unreachability facts, not because nothing reads it.
